claims.text: AWS's AI business and its chips business (including custom Trainium and Graviton silicon) each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Microsoft's Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for fiscal year 2026, the first time.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Gartner says by 2028 cloud-native platforms will be the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
AWS posted $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest growth since 2021.
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Gartner predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Gartner says by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.
Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said developers are standardizing on CNCF projects and organizations are extending platforms to support AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 82% agree AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.
In Pulumi's survey, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes, yet manual approval remains close to universal; the report describes this as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's survey, teams expecting agents to generate half or more of infrastructure code rise from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails.
Mordor Intelligence values the global Kubernetes market at USD 3.13 billion in 2026, projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%, with 30% of backend developers using Kubernetes directly, down from a 36% peak in Q3 2023, which the report attributes to maturity.
Pulumi published a comparison of Kubernetes IaC tools at /blog/best-kubernetes-iac-tools-2026/.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a generally available MCP server for its Agent Toolkit, and Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server.
Gartner says by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Unified governance, modern IaC, reusable components and policy frameworks are core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
Last year's edition predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade and the 2026 predictions held up.
